issues.quote: even though `UseAuthentication` itself never rejects a request
issues.text: Unlisted claim: an absolute behavioural statement about a framework component that appears in no entry of .meta.json claims (claims 1-8 never mention UseAuthentication). The documentation does support it - "Authentication doesn't short-circuit unauthenticated requests. Although authentication middleware authenticates requests, authorization occurs after the framework selects ... a controller and action in an MVC app." - so the sentence may stay as written, but the ledger hides that it was checked.
issues.fix: Add to .meta.json claims: {"n": 9, "text": "UseAuthentication identifies the caller and does not itself short-circuit or reject a request; UseAuthorization is the step that rejects.", "kind": "behavior", "version_key": "aspnetcore", "source_hint": "ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware fundamentals: 'Authentication doesn't short-circuit unauthenticated requests'", "needs_verification": true, "section": 5}. No change needed to the lesson text.

issues.quote: it runs before any middleware and has no line of its own in `Program.cs`
issues.text: "before any middleware" is too strong on two counts. Routing is itself middleware - middleware/index.md: "If you don't call `app.UseRouting`, the Routing middleware runs at the beginning of the pipeline by default" - and it is not always first: "UseDeveloperExceptionPage is added first when the HostingEnvironment is 'Development'. UseRouting is added second". The lab's api container runs with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development (its log prints "Hosting environment: Development"), so a middleware does run before routing there. The second half is correct: Program.cs never calls UseRouting.
issues.fix: Narrow it to what the lesson needs: "routing - the automatic step that decides which endpoint a request's path and method match; it runs before any of the middleware registered in `Program.cs`, and has no line of its own there."

issues.quote: `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` and `RequestLoggingMiddleware` — both registered before it — still run their after-`next` code
issues.text: Untrue of ExceptionHandlingMiddleware as written at stage-1: it has no after-`next` code. Its whole body is try { await next(context); } catch (KeyNotFoundException ex) {...} catch (ArgumentException ex) {...} catch (Exception ex) {...} - nothing follows the await inside the try, and nothing follows the try/catch. On a 401 it executes no statement on the way out; control simply returns through it. RequestLoggingMiddleware is the only one of the two with code after `next`.
issues.fix: Say what is true of both: "...control still returns through `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` and `RequestLoggingMiddleware` - both registered before it - because from where they stand, `next` returned: the logger runs its after-`next` code and logs the 401, and the exception handler's `try` block simply finishes with nothing to catch."

issues.quote: but travels out through `RequestLoggingMiddleware` and `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` regardless — as you saw in the previous lesson's Try it.
issues.text: The citation covers only half the sentence. backend.l1.middleware-pipeline's Try it yields one observable fact - "curl prints `401`; the log line still reads `POST /api/v1/orders responded 401 in ...ms`" - which is the RequestLoggingMiddleware half. Nothing in that Try it shows (or could show) ExceptionHandlingMiddleware on the way out: it writes and logs nothing unless an exception is thrown. "As you saw" over-reaches for the second name.
issues.fix: Attach the citation to what was observed: "...but travels out through `RequestLoggingMiddleware` - which is why the previous lesson's Try it still found `POST /api/v1/orders responded 401` in the log - and through `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` before it, which has nothing to do on the way out of a request that threw nothing."

issues.quote: but `app.MapControllers()`, the line that runs whichever method was matched
issues.text: `app.MapControllers()` registers the controller endpoints; it is not itself the step that runs the matched method. Docs (middleware8.md, >= aspnetcore-8.0): "UseEndpoints is added at the end of the middleware pipeline if endpoints are configured" and "User configured middleware and endpoints are added between UseRouting and UseEndpoints" - the matched endpoint is executed there. The prerequisite lesson puts it correctly: "`app.MapControllers()` registers endpoints, which are invoked only after every middleware has run." Ordering is unaffected: it is the last of the six lines.
issues.fix: Use the prereq's wording: "...but `app.MapControllers()`, the line that registers the controller methods as endpoints - the last of the six, where whichever method was matched actually runs."
